payload.title: 10 Rhodes Wedding Venues From Lindos to the Old Town
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning an intimate to mid-sized guest list flying in from Australia. They have chosen Rhodes (or are weighing it against Santorini, Mykonos and Crete) for its mix of medieval Old Town, Lindos and long beaches, and now need to decide which part of the island suits them (Lindos and the south-east, the Old Town and Rhodes city, the east coast or the west coast) and shortlist venues compared on the same terms: setting, ceremony options, capacity, rooms and exclusive use.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can check availability, ceremony options and house rules for the couple's shortlisted Rhodes venues on their dates and guest count.
payload.angle: Rhodes is two weddings in one island: the whitewashed village and bays of Lindos in the south-east, and the walled medieval Old Town in the north, with resort coasts either side. Most Rhodes lists blur these together. This guide groups 10 venues by area, from Lindos and the south-east through the east coast to the Old Town and Rhodes city and the west coast, and every venue is included only because its own official site, read live, says it hosts weddings. Each entry gives the same fields in the same order: setting, ceremony options as stated, capacity, rooms and exclusive use (else 'Not published'), and one standout. No ranking: the order follows the island, so a couple can choose an area first and a venue second.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: Rhodes' four wedding areas (Lindos and the south-east; the Old Town and Rhodes city; the east coast; the west coast) and that the right one depends on guest count, ceremony type and setting; link the hub /destinations/europe/greece and /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues.
At a glance: mobile-friendly comparison table with 5 columns (venue, area, setting, ceremony options, capacity), 'Not published' where a field is not published.

How to compare like for like: venue type (resort, boutique hotel in the Old Town, private or historic venue), ceremony on site, seated capacity, rooms on site, exclusive use. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (house rules not published are confirmed in writing by the Wedded Advisor), plus a link to /wonderland-concierge.
Choosing an area: practical guidance per area as official tourism or venue sources state it; no unsourced distances, drive times or sunset claims.

Inclusion rule applied to every entry: a live read of the venue's own official site says it hosts weddings. Never snippets alone. Target 10; if fewer qualify the title count changes and the person is told; no padding. Non-luxury qualifiers held as reserves. Include Lindos venues and at least one Old Town (medieval town) venue if any qualify. Public monuments named only as settings, as an official source describes them; civil ceremony locations go in the legal section, not the count.

10 venues grouped by area (Lindos and the south-east: St Paul's Bay, Vlicha, Pefkos; the Old Town and Rhodes city; the east coast: Kallithea, Faliraki, Kolymbia, Tsambika; the west coast: Ixia, Ialysos, Kalavarda), each with the same fields in the same order: setting; ceremony options as stated; capacity, rooms and exclusive use where published, else 'Not published'; one standout. No ranking or rank-implying numbering.
Getting there: Rhodes airport and port from official sources (airport operator, port or Visit Greece); Smartraveller ferry advice only; no transfer arrangements.
When to marry: HNMS Rodos station averages, labelled; Smartraveller heat, wildfire and swimming advice; no 'best month'.

Legal in brief, as at November 2026, dated once: Embassy Athens and Smartraveller; Municipality of Rhodes civil steps only if an official page is read live, else 'check with the municipality and the embassy, including any fees'; link the Greece venues guide's legal section; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once. Nothing on church or religious paperwork.

FAQ (4 to 6): Which part of Rhodes suits a wedding? Can we marry in Rhodes Old Town? Can we book a Rhodes venue for exclusive use? How do guests get to Rhodes? Can Australians legally marry in Rhodes?

Close: shortlist with a Wedded Advisor (brand-facts claims only). Links: /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destinations/europe/greece, /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=rhodes-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Any price, fee, minimum spend or amount; 'free'; any capacity, room count, distance or time not on an official source.
'Best' or ranking claims; numbering that implies rank; 'best month'.
Venues without a weddings offer on their own official site; venues off Rhodes; public monuments or civil ceremony locations counted as venues.

Research talk in copy ('on its own site', 'in its own words', what we could or could not confirm, myths); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once; linking a source more than once.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, booking or review sites, Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.
Vendor names other than venues; venue contact or business details; transfer arrangements; implying partnerships or preferred rates.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Wedded Advisor definition line in brand-facts.md (never reuse it or its closing phrase); 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text; legal, church or religious paperwork detail.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; images other than placeholders.
